bug_semantics: An authenticated platform administrator could send PUT /api/users/{username} for a different, non-admin user with PlatformRoleID set to SuperAdminRole. The handler authorized admins to update ordinary users and rejected assignment of AdminRole, but had no equivalent rejection for SuperAdminRole; logic.UpdateUser then copied the attacker-controlled PlatformRoleID into the stored user, yielding platform super-admin privilege.
flaw_origin: Commit 78da9fa9010ba568d6d6c84ef856e559571d01e6 migrated the update path from legacy IsAdmin booleans to role IDs. It changed logic/auth.go to persist userchange.PlatformRoleID verbatim and rewrote the handler checks to role IDs, but the non-self admin branch only rejected a requested AdminRole and omitted a requested SuperAdminRole. Its immediate parent 34bcff2b1d68ab6f32e8ae36b939fdeb42682eff persisted only userchange.IsAdmin and did not copy IsSuperAdmin or PlatformRoleID, so the advisory's role-ID escalation mechanism was absent there.
ai_marker: absent: git cat-file commit 78da9fa9010ba568d6d6c84ef856e559571d01e6 shows author and committer abhishek9686 <abhi281342@gmail.com>, subject 'use new role id for user apis', and no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI trailer
evidence: GitHub advisory API GHSA-ch3w-9456-38v3 and the PUBLISHED CVE.org record CVE-2026-29195 describe CWE-863 in PUT /api/users/{username}: an admin can assign the super-admin role; neither record is withdrawn or rejected.

git show 78da9fa9010ba568d6d6c84ef856e559571d01e6:controllers/user.go lines 788-809 shows the vulnerable authorization path: an AdminRole caller may update a non-admin target, and the requested-role guard rejects only userchange.PlatformRoleID == AdminRole, not SuperAdminRole.

git show 78da9fa9010ba568d6d6c84ef856e559571d01e6:logic/auth.go lines 238-242 shows the sink user.PlatformRoleID = userchange.PlatformRoleID followed by validation, so the accepted super-admin role is persisted.

Immediate-parent tree check: git show 34bcff2b1d68ab6f32e8ae36b939fdeb42682eff:logic/auth.go lines 238-242 writes only user.IsAdmin = userchange.IsAdmin; it does not copy IsSuperAdmin or PlatformRoleID. git diff 34bcff2b1d68ab6f32e8ae36b939fdeb42682eff 78da9fa9010ba568d6d6c84ef856e559571d01e6 confirms the vulnerable role-ID write and matching incomplete guard first appear in the BIC.

git cat-file commit 78da9fa9010ba568d6d6c84ef856e559571d01e6 gives the single parent 34bcff2b1d68ab6f32e8ae36b939fdeb42682eff, human author/committer abhishek9686 <abhi281342@gmail.com>, and no trailers; the BIC is an atomic non-merge commit, not a squash aggregate.

Direct fix 168ef57faf2943d2e4c095420d276aac084dec1b adds controllers/user.go lines 1316-1329 rejecting userchange.PlatformRoleID == SuperAdminRole on the ordinary update endpoint; follow-up 8422933cfb51b6728b0460ec4e1b107baa32a3e7 narrows the condition to actual role changes so an existing super-admin can still update non-role fields.

Topology check: merge commit 0d938931c0fd3a703abbb6b7c46fe64c751ae183 contains direct fix 168ef57faf2943d2e4c095420d276aac084dec1b; git tag --contains shows both the direct fix and follow-up first in v1.5.1 and v1.6.0.

Release cross-check found a first-party metadata discrepancy: GitHub/CVE.org claim first patched version 1.5.0, but git merge-base --is-ancestor shows v1.5.0 contains BIC 78da9fa9010ba568d6d6c84ef856e559571d01e6 and contains neither 168ef57faf2943d2e4c095420d276aac084dec1b nor 8422933cfb51b6728b0460ec4e1b107baa32a3e7; v1.5.1 contains all three. The GitHub v1.5.0 release was published 2026-02-11, before the 2026-02-25 direct fix.
reasoning: The advisory is a real, published authorization vulnerability. The complete attack path is an authenticated AdminRole caller updating another ordinary user, the handler permitting that caller and rejecting only requested AdminRole, and logic.UpdateUser persisting the requested SuperAdminRole. Commit 78da9fa9010ba568d6d6c84ef856e559571d01e6 is the smallest public commit that first completes this mechanism: its immediate parent uses the legacy boolean write and cannot persist the requested super-admin role, while the BIC simultaneously introduces the PlatformRoleID sink and the incomplete role-ID guard. The non-merge BIC needs no squash decomposition. Commit 168ef57faf2943d2e4c095420d276aac084dec1b directly blocks SuperAdminRole on this endpoint, merge 0d938931c0fd3a703abbb6b7c46fe64c751ae183 integrates it, and 8422933cfb51b6728b0460ec4e1b107baa32a3e7 preserves that block only for actual role changes. Tag topology contradicts the advisory's claimed v1.5.0 patched boundary and instead identifies v1.5.1 as the first tagged fixed tree; this does not leave the source-level BIC, fix, or authorship uncertain. The BIC commit object has a human author/committer and no AI marker, so the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
